audit_scope.description: These subgraphs cover EL concerns (EVM precompile validation via EIP-7823, transaction gas limit enforcement via EIP-7825) and CL/networking concerns (PeerDAS data availability sampling via EIP-7594). Both layers are in scope.

out_of_scope_reasons.Mainnet/Testnet Testing: All testing should be done on local forks of testnet or mainnet
out_of_scope_reasons.Pricing Oracles: Incorrect data supplied by third party oracles (oracle manipulation/flash loan attacks are in-scope)
out_of_scope_reasons.Third-party Smart Contracts: Any testing with third-party systems and applications is prohibited
out_of_scope_reasons.Test Files: Impacts on test files and configuration files unless stated otherwise
out_of_scope_reasons.Privileged Access: Impacts caused by attacks requiring access to privileged addresses without additional modifications are out-of-scope
out_of_scope_reasons.Centralization Risks: Impacts involving centralization risks are out-of-scope

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Nodes via P2P Network (DAS Sampling)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes on the P2P network are unauthenticated. They may provide invalid column data, withhold data, or attempt eclipse attacks. All received column data must be verified via KZG proofs.

trusted_external_entities.name: Blob Transaction Submitter via P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Blob transaction gossip (network wrapper with blobs, commitments, cell_proofs)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Blob transactions arrive via unauthenticated P2P gossip. All fields (blob count, quantity matching, cell proof count, KZG hashes, cell proofs) must be fully validated before acceptance.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Column Custodians via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers responding to missing column requests are unauthenticated. They may provide invalid columns or refuse to respond. Erasure coding reconstruction and KZG proof verification are required.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via Transaction Submission (Blob TX Gossip)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Transaction submission (RPC or P2P) for blob transactions
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users submitting blob transactions are untrusted. Transaction wrapper format, cell proofs, and all blob data must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract/EOA Caller via EVM MODEXP Precompile
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any contract or EOA can invoke the MODEXP precompile with arbitrary input data. Input length parameters (BASE, EXPONENT, MODULUS) must each be validated against the 1024-byte cap before processing.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender via RPC/P2P (Gas Limit)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Transaction submission (eth_sendRawTransaction RPC or P2P gossip)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Transaction senders can set arbitrary gasLimit values. The gasLimit field must be validated against the 16,777,216 cap at both mempool admission and block validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P (Block Propagation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes broadcasting blocks are untrusted. Blocks may contain transactions with gasLimit exceeding the cap. Each transaction in a received block must be validated against the gas cap.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Actor via MODEXP Large Input
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EVM CALL to precompile address 0x05 with oversized inputs
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attackers may craft transactions calling MODEXP with inputs exceeding 1024 bytes to trigger consensus bugs or resource exhaustion across client implementations. Immediate rejection at length check is required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Actor via High-Gas Transaction DoS
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Transaction submission with gasLimit exceeding cap
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attackers may submit transactions with extremely high gas limits to exhaust node resources during validation. The 16,777,216 cap enforces bounded validation time.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All received column samples must be verified via batch KZG proof verification before being used for data availability determination. Invalid or missing proofs must result in treating data as unavailable.

Full validation required: blob count <= 6, quantity matching (versioned hashes == blobs == commitments), cell proof count == CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB * len(blobs), KZG commitment-to-hash verification, batch cell proof verification. Reject on any failure.

Columns received from custodian peers must be KZG-proof verified. Reconstruction should only proceed when >= 50% of columns are available and verified. Timeout handling must prevent indefinite blocking.
Blob transaction wrapper format must be validated including wrapper_version, proof structure, and all cryptographic commitments before pool admission.

length_of_BASE, length_of_EXPONENT, and length_of_MODULUS must each be validated <= 1024 bytes before any computation. On violation: consume all gas and return error. Check must be identical across all client implementations to prevent consensus failures.
Transaction gasLimit must be validated <= 16,777,216 (2^24) at mempool admission. Transactions exceeding the cap must be rejected immediately.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Block validation transaction gas limit check
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Every transaction in a received block must have gasLimit validated <= 16,777,216. Blocks containing any transaction exceeding the cap must be rejected as invalid.
Oversized inputs must be rejected at the length check stage before any complex computation (pricing, modular exponentiation). All gas must be consumed as penalty.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Transaction pool and block validation gas cap enforcement
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Gas cap enforcement must occur early in validation to prevent resource exhaustion. Both mempool and block-level validation must independently enforce the cap.
